# Purpose and analytic boundaries

This is a **visualization-only amendment to Notebook 07**. It reads the saved `07_scored_2025` checkpoint and evaluates the **entire eligible 2025 respondent sample**, irrespective of race, AI/AN status, or whether race was resolved. It uses the **same three pre-existing, historically trained and 2024-calibrated probability predictions**: logistic regression, LASSO, and random forest.

**No model fitting, recalibration, model selection, or threshold tuning occurs here.** This notebook does not change previous project outputs. It creates three **separate ROC figures**, three **separate precision–recall figures**, and three **separate confusion matrices**, plus useful comparative visualizations, metric tables, and audit tables.

- **ROC / AUROC:** Weighted discrimination across all thresholds; no cutoff required.
- **Precision–recall / weighted average precision (AP):** Performance for the positive class (FMD), particularly useful with unequal class prevalence.
- **F1, precision, recall, specificity, accuracy, confusion matrices:** Depend on a **pre-specified cutoff of 0.50**. This is a reporting convention, **not a threshold optimized on the 2025 evaluation data**. With an FMD prevalence near 16%, a 0.50 cutoff may be conservative and produce relatively few positive classifications.
- **Brier score and calibration:** Evaluate prediction probabilities rather than thresholded decisions.
- **Survey design:** Survey weights (`RAW_WEIGHT`) are used for all primary metrics. Graphs and metrics here do not estimate confidence intervals or incorporate PSU/stratum uncertainty. The notebook's 2025 data have already been examined in prior exploratory work; these are later-year / out-of-time **post-hoc** analyses, not an untouched prospective evaluation.

## 1. Attach to the existing run

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
    current <- normalizePath(start, mustWork = TRUE)
    repeat {
        if (file.exists(file.path(current, "FMD_Project.Rproj"))) return(current)
        parent <- dirname(current)
        if (identical(parent, current)) stop("Open FMD_Project.Rproj in RStudio first.")
        current <- parent
    }
}
project_root <- find_project_root()
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)

# Matches the loader used by Notebooks 07 and 08.
load_module <- function(name) {
    path <- file.path(project_root, "R", paste0(name, ".Rmd"))
    lines <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
    starts <- which(startsWith(lines, "```{r"))
    ends <- which(trimws(lines) == "```")
    blocks <- lapply(starts, function(start) {
        finish <- ends[ends > start][1L]
        if (is.na(finish) || finish <= start + 1L) stop("Malformed R chunk: ", path)
        paste(lines[(start + 1L):(finish - 1L)], collapse = "\n")
    })
    eval(parse(text = paste(blocks, collapse = "\n\n")), envir = parent.frame())
    invisible(TRUE)
}

load_module("config")
load_module("run_manager")
load_module("helpers")
load_module("plot_palette")
run_context <- attach_run()  # attaches; does not create a new run
check_packages(c("data.table", "ggplot2"))
cat("[07b] Attached run:", run_context$id, "\n")
```

## 2. Load and audit the complete 2025 scoring checkpoint

```{r load-national-2025, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
scored <- data.table::as.data.table(load_run_rds("checkpoints", "07_scored_2025"))
needed <- c("YEAR", "FMD", "RAW_WEIGHT", "prob_logistic", "prob_lasso", "prob_forest")
missing_cols <- setdiff(needed, names(scored))
if (length(missing_cols)) stop("Missing columns in Notebook 07 checkpoint: ",
                               paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))
if (!nrow(scored) || anyNA(scored$YEAR) || !all(as.integer(scored$YEAR) == 2025L)) {
    stop("Expected a nonempty checkpoint containing only 2025 observations.")
}

# There is deliberately NO race/cohort selection here.
eligible <- data.table::copy(scored[valid_outcome(FMD) & valid_weight(RAW_WEIGHT)])
if (!nrow(eligible)) stop("No 2025 respondents have valid FMD outcomes and weights.")
eligible[, y_binary := as.numeric(as.character(FMD))]
if (anyNA(eligible$y_binary) || !all(eligible$y_binary %in% c(0, 1))) {
    stop("FMD must be coded 0/1 for binary classification metrics.")
}
if (data.table::uniqueN(eligible$y_binary) != 2L) stop("Both FMD classes must be present.")

families <- c("logistic", "lasso", "forest")
model_names <- c(logistic = "Logistic regression", lasso = "LASSO", forest = "Random forest")
model_colors <- c(logistic = "#2D9E98", lasso = "#B66D46", forest = "#C59B50")
positive_color <- "#B66D46"
negative_color <- "#2D9E98"
for (family in families) {
    p <- eligible[[paste0("prob_", family)]]
    if (!is.numeric(p) || any(!is.finite(p)) || any(p < 0 | p > 1)) {
        stop("Invalid 2025 probabilities for ", family, ".")
    }
}

n_eligible <- nrow(eligible)
y <- eligible$y_binary
w <- eligible$RAW_WEIGHT
weighted_prevalence <- sum(w * y) / sum(w)
threshold_fixed <- 0.50  # CHOSEN A PRIORI; never optimized on 2025

audit <- data.table::data.table(
    item = c("2025 scored records", "Eligible known-outcome and positive-weight records",
             "Excluded from metrics", "Unweighted FMD-positive count",
             "Unweighted FMD-negative count", "Survey-weighted FMD prevalence",
             "Fixed classification threshold"),
    value = c(nrow(scored), n_eligible, nrow(scored) - n_eligible,
              sum(y == 1), sum(y == 0),
              sprintf("%.4f (%.2f%%)", weighted_prevalence, 100 * weighted_prevalence),
              sprintf("%.2f", threshold_fixed))
)
print(audit)
save_table(audit, "07b_national_2025_cohort_audit")
cat("[07b] Race/cohort columns, if present, were NOT used to restrict eligibility.\n")
```

## 3. Define reproducible, survey-weighted metrics

**Definitions:** Recall / sensitivity = TP/(TP+FN); specificity = TN/(TN+FP); precision = TP/(TP+FP); F1 = harmonic mean of precision and recall. A displayed confusion matrix is **row-normalized by actual outcome using survey weights** and also reports unweighted respondent counts. Weighted cell totals are weighted population totals, not counts of individual survey participants.

```{r weighted-metric-functions}
safe_ratio <- function(numerator, denominator, default = 0) {
    if (!is.finite(denominator) || denominator <= 0) return(default)
    numerator / denominator
}

weighted_confusion <- function(y, p, w, threshold = 0.5) {
    predicted <- as.integer(p >= threshold)
    tp <- sum(w[y == 1 & predicted == 1]); fn <- sum(w[y == 1 & predicted == 0])
    fp <- sum(w[y == 0 & predicted == 1]); tn <- sum(w[y == 0 & predicted == 0])
    n_tp <- sum(y == 1 & predicted == 1); n_fn <- sum(y == 1 & predicted == 0)
    n_fp <- sum(y == 0 & predicted == 1); n_tn <- sum(y == 0 & predicted == 0)
    precision <- safe_ratio(tp, tp + fp)
    recall <- safe_ratio(tp, tp + fn)
    specificity <- safe_ratio(tn, tn + fp)
    f1 <- safe_ratio(2 * precision * recall, precision + recall)
    balanced_accuracy <- (recall + specificity) / 2
    metrics <- data.table::data.table(
        threshold = threshold,
        weighted_accuracy = safe_ratio(tp + tn, tp + tn + fp + fn),
        weighted_balanced_accuracy = balanced_accuracy,
        weighted_precision = precision,
        weighted_recall = recall,
        weighted_specificity = specificity,
        weighted_f1 = f1,
        weighted_false_positive_rate = 1 - specificity,
        weighted_predicted_positive_fraction = safe_ratio(tp + fp, tp + fn + fp + tn)
    )
    cells <- data.table::data.table(
        actual = c("No FMD", "No FMD", "FMD", "FMD"),
        predicted = c("No FMD", "FMD", "No FMD", "FMD"),
        cell = c("TN", "FP", "FN", "TP"),
        n_respondents = c(n_tn, n_fp, n_fn, n_tp),
        weighted_total = c(tn, fp, fn, tp),
        weighted_row_percent = 100 * c(
            safe_ratio(tn, tn + fp), safe_ratio(fp, tn + fp),
            safe_ratio(fn, fn + tp), safe_ratio(tp, fn + tp))
    )
    list(metrics = metrics, cells = cells)
}

# Compute weighted ROC and weighted precision-recall coordinates at each
# DISTINCT prediction threshold.  Equal scores are handled together; this
# avoids an arbitrary ordering of tied scores.
weighted_binary_curves <- function(y, p, w) {
    data <- data.table::data.table(score = p, y = as.integer(y), w = w)
    pts <- data[, .(positive_w = sum(w[y == 1L]),
                    negative_w = sum(w[y == 0L])), by = score]
    data.table::setorder(pts, -score)
    Wpos <- sum(w[y == 1L]); Wneg <- sum(w[y == 0L])
    pts[, tp_w := cumsum(positive_w)]
    pts[, fp_w := cumsum(negative_w)]
    pts[, tn_w := Wneg - fp_w]
    pts[, fn_w := Wpos - tp_w]
    pts[, tpr := tp_w / Wpos]
    pts[, fpr := fp_w / Wneg]
    pts[, recall := tpr]
    pts[, precision := tp_w / pmax(tp_w + fp_w, .Machine$double.eps)]
    pts[, f1 := 2 * precision * recall / pmax(precision + recall, .Machine$double.eps)]
    pts[, threshold := score]
    origin <- data.table::data.table(
        score = Inf, positive_w = 0, negative_w = 0,
        tp_w = 0, fp_w = 0, tn_w = Wneg, fn_w = Wpos,
        tpr = 0, fpr = 0, recall = 0, precision = 1, f1 = 0,
        threshold = Inf
    )
    pts <- data.table::rbindlist(list(origin, pts), use.names = TRUE)
    pts[, tpr := pmin(1, pmax(0, tpr))]
    pts[, fpr := pmin(1, pmax(0, fpr))]
    pts[, recall := pmin(1, pmax(0, recall))]
    pts[, precision := pmin(1, pmax(0, precision))]
    n <- nrow(pts)
    auc_trapezoid <- sum(diff(pts$fpr) * (pts$tpr[-1] + pts$tpr[-n]) / 2)
    # Weighted average precision: stepwise precision-recall integration.
    ap <- sum(pmax(0, diff(pts$recall)) * pts$precision[-1])
    list(points = pts, auc_from_curve = auc_trapezoid, average_precision = ap)
}

# For plotting only. Full, unthinned predictions are used in all metrics.
thin_points <- function(points, max_points = 2200L) {
    n <- nrow(points)
    if (n <= max_points) return(points)
    keep <- unique(c(seq_len(min(n, 80L)),
                     as.integer(round(seq(1, n, length.out = max_points))), n))
    points[sort(keep)]
}

weighted_logloss <- function(y, p, w) {
    eps <- 1e-12
    p <- pmin(1 - eps, pmax(eps, p))
    sum(w * (-y * log(p) - (1 - y) * log1p(-p))) / sum(w)
}
```

## 4. Compute model-level results using **all** eligible respondents

```{r compute-national-metrics, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
all_curves <- list()
metrics <- list()
threshold_metrics <- list()
confusion_cells <- list()

for (family in families) {
    p <- eligible[[paste0("prob_", family)]]
    curve <- weighted_binary_curves(y, p, w)
    auc_project <- weighted_auc(y, p, w)  # exactly the established project metric
    if (abs(auc_project - curve$auc_from_curve) > 1e-4) {
        warning("Project weighted_auc and weighted ROC integral differ for ", family,
                ": ", round(auc_project, 6), " vs ", round(curve$auc_from_curve, 6))
    }
    conf <- weighted_confusion(y, p, w, threshold_fixed)
    all_curves[[family]] <- curve$points
    metrics[[family]] <- data.table::data.table(
        family = family,
        model = model_names[[family]],
        respondents = n_eligible,
        weighted_auroc = auc_project,
        weighted_average_precision = curve$average_precision,
        weighted_brier = sum(w * (p - y)^2) / sum(w),
        weighted_logloss = weighted_logloss(y, p, w),
        weighted_observed_fmd = weighted_prevalence,
        weighted_mean_predicted_fmd = sum(w * p) / sum(w),
        calibration_in_large = sum(w * (p - y)) / sum(w)
    )
    threshold_metrics[[family]] <- data.table::copy(conf$metrics)[,
        `:=`(family = family, model = model_names[[family]])]
    confusion_cells[[family]] <- data.table::copy(conf$cells)[,
        `:=`(family = family, model = model_names[[family]])]
}
metric_table <- data.table::rbindlist(metrics)
threshold_table <- data.table::rbindlist(threshold_metrics)
confusion_table <- data.table::rbindlist(confusion_cells)
report_table <- merge(metric_table, threshold_table,
                      by = c("family", "model"), sort = FALSE)
report_table <- report_table[match(families, family)]

print(report_table[, .(model, respondents, weighted_auroc,
                       weighted_average_precision, weighted_brier,
                       weighted_precision, weighted_recall, weighted_f1,
                       weighted_specificity, weighted_accuracy)])
print(confusion_table)
save_table(report_table, "07b_2025_all_models_full_metrics")
save_table(confusion_table, "07b_2025_weighted_confusion_matrices")

# Keep the national 2023-selected model identified, without reselecting it.
selected <- load_run_rds("models", "05_frozen_selection")
cat("[07b] 2023-selected family:", selected$chosen_family, "\n")
cat("[07b] Weighted 2025 FMD prevalence:", round(100 * weighted_prevalence, 2), "%\n")
cat("[07b] Fixed threshold:", threshold_fixed,
    "; results must NOT be described as threshold-optimized.\n")
```

## 5. Three **separate** ROC figures (AUROC)

Each plot uses the full eligible 2025 population, irrespective of race, with a distinct standalone image for each model. The diagonal shows chance-level discrimination. Only the display coordinates are thinned; AUROC is computed from all eligible weighted predictions.

```{r three-separate-rocs, fig.width=8, fig.height=6, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
for (family in families) {
    pts <- thin_points(all_curves[[family]])
    auc <- metrics[[family]]$weighted_auroc
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(pts, ggplot2::aes(fpr, tpr)) +
        ggplot2::geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
                             color = "#D5C7BC", linewidth = 0.85) +
        ggplot2::geom_line(color = model_colors[[family]], linewidth = 1.4) +
        ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2)) +
        ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2)) +
        ggplot2::coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), expand = FALSE) +
        atg_theme() +
        ggplot2::labs(
            title = paste0("2025 national ROC — ", model_names[[family]]),
            subtitle = sprintf("Survey-weighted AUROC = %.4f | n = %s (all races)",
                               auc, format(n_eligible, big.mark = ",")),
            x = "False positive rate (1 − specificity)",
            y = "True positive rate (sensitivity)",
            caption = "2025 outcomes; frozen model and 2024 calibration. Dashed line = chance."
        )
    show_and_save(p, paste0("07b_2025_national_roc_", family), 8, 6)
}
```

## 7. Three **separate** precision–recall curves

The positive class is FMD. The dotted horizontal reference is 2025 weighted FMD prevalence. The reported PR summary is **weighted average precision (AP)**, a stepwise precision–recall integral, not ROC AUROC.

```{r three-separate-pr, fig.width=8, fig.height=6, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
for (family in families) {
    pts <- thin_points(all_curves[[family]])
    ap <- metrics[[family]]$weighted_average_precision
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(pts, ggplot2::aes(recall, precision)) +
        ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = weighted_prevalence,
                            linetype = "dashed", color = "#BFA58D") +
        ggplot2::geom_line(color = model_colors[[family]], linewidth = 1.25) +
        ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, .2)) +
        ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, .2)) +
        ggplot2::coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), expand = FALSE) +
        atg_theme() +
        ggplot2::labs(title = paste0("2025 precision–recall — ", model_names[[family]]),
                      subtitle = sprintf("Weighted average precision = %.4f | FMD prevalence = %.1f%%",
                                         ap, 100 * weighted_prevalence),
                      x = "Recall (sensitivity)", y = "Precision (positive predictive value)",
                      caption = "Curve thinned for display; weighted AP uses all prediction thresholds.")
    show_and_save(p, paste0("07b_2025_national_pr_", family), 8, 6)
}
```

## 9. Three **separate** weighted confusion matrices at threshold 0.50

Every heatmap shows **weighted conditional percentages within the actual outcome row**, along with **unweighted respondent counts**. A 50% cutoff is a fixed illustration and was **not** optimized on this evaluation set.

```{r three-confusion-matrices, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=6, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
for (family in families) {
    cm <- data.table::copy(confusion_cells[[family]])
    cm[, actual := factor(actual, levels = c("FMD", "No FMD"))]
    cm[, predicted := factor(predicted, levels = c("No FMD", "FMD"))]
    cm[, display := sprintf("%s\n%.1f%% of actual class\n(n = %s)",
                            cell, weighted_row_percent,
                            format(n_respondents, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE))]
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(cm, ggplot2::aes(predicted, actual,
                                         fill = weighted_row_percent)) +
        ggplot2::geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1.5) +
        ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = display), size = 4.2,
                           lineheight = 1.12, color = "#44362E") +
        ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F4E9DF", high = "#6CBEB6",
                                     limits = c(0, 100), name = "Weighted row %") +
        ggplot2::coord_equal() +
        atg_theme() +
        ggplot2::theme(panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank()) +
        ggplot2::labs(title = paste0("2025 confusion matrix — ", model_names[[family]]),
                      subtitle = "All races | Fixed threshold = 0.50",
                      x = "Predicted class", y = "Actual FMD status",
                      caption = "Cell percentages are weighted within each actual class; n are unweighted respondents.")
    show_and_save(p, paste0("07b_2025_national_confusion_", family), 7.5, 6)
}
```

## 10. F1, precision, recall and specificity comparison (fixed 0.50 threshold)

```{r classification-metrics-comparison, fig.width=11, fig.height=6, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
classification_long <- data.table::melt(
    threshold_table,
    id.vars = c("family", "model", "threshold"),
    measure.vars = c("weighted_precision", "weighted_recall", "weighted_f1",
                     "weighted_specificity"),
    variable.name = "metric", value.name = "score"
)
classification_long[, metric := factor(metric,
    levels = c("weighted_precision", "weighted_recall", "weighted_f1",
               "weighted_specificity"),
    labels = c("Precision", "Recall / sensitivity", "F1 score", "Specificity"))]
classification_long[, model := factor(model, levels = unname(model_names[families]))]
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(classification_long,
                     ggplot2::aes(x = model, y = score, fill = family)) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(width = .64) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", score)),
                       vjust = -0.28, size = 3.4) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~metric, nrow = 2) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = model_colors) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.07), breaks = seq(0, 1, .25)) +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 18, hjust = 1),
                   legend.position = "none") +
    ggplot2::labs(title = "2025 national classification metrics at threshold 0.50",
                  subtitle = "Survey-weighted | Positive class: frequent mental distress",
                  x = NULL, y = "Metric value (0–1)",
                  caption = "Classification metrics depend on threshold. 0.50 was not tuned on 2025 outcomes.")
show_and_save(p, "07b_2025_national_f1_precision_recall_specificity", 11, 6)

## 11. Threshold sensitivity (descriptive only; do not select a cutoff using 2025)

These charts show **how** the three threshold-dependent metrics would vary under different hypothetical cutoffs. They are **diagnostic**, not a permissible procedure for choosing a new 2025 test-set threshold.

```{r threshold-sensitivity, fig.width=11, fig.height=6, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
grid <- seq(0.05, 0.95, by = 0.025)
threshold_sweep <- data.table::rbindlist(lapply(families, function(family) {
    p <- eligible[[paste0("prob_", family)]]
    data.table::rbindlist(lapply(grid, function(t) {
        z <- weighted_confusion(y, p, w, t)$metrics
        z[, `:=`(family = family, model = model_names[[family]])]
        z
    }))
}))
save_table(threshold_sweep, "07b_2025_national_threshold_sensitivity")
sweep_long <- data.table::melt(threshold_sweep,
    id.vars = c("family", "model", "threshold"),
    measure.vars = c("weighted_precision", "weighted_recall", "weighted_f1"),
    variable.name = "metric", value.name = "score")
sweep_long[, metric := factor(metric,
    levels = c("weighted_precision", "weighted_recall", "weighted_f1"),
    labels = c("Precision", "Recall", "F1"))]
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(sweep_long,
                     ggplot2::aes(threshold, score, color = metric)) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1.05) +
    ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = threshold_fixed, linetype = "dashed",
                        color = "#9F9084") +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~model, nrow = 1) +
    ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = c("Precision" = "#B66D46",
                                           "Recall" = "#2D9E98",
                                           "F1" = "#6E584B")) +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(title = "2025 threshold sensitivity — diagnostic only",
                  subtitle = "Dashed line = fixed reported threshold (0.50)",
                  x = "Hypothetical probability threshold", y = "Survey-weighted metric",
                  color = "Metric",
                  caption = "Do not choose a new threshold by maximizing 2025 F1; tune on earlier data instead.")
show_and_save(p, "07b_2025_national_threshold_sensitivity", 11, 6)
```

## 12. Probability calibration curves (weighted within 2025 risk bins)

For each model, predictions are grouped into **up to ten unweighted-count risk quantile bins**, while each bin's reported predicted and observed FMD rates use the respondent survey weights. Tied probabilities are not artificially split; some models may have fewer than ten groups. Points here are **descriptive** and have no confidence intervals.

```{r probability-calibration, fig.width=11, fig.height=6, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
calibration_rows <- list()
for (family in families) {
    p <- eligible[[paste0("prob_", family)]]
    cuts <- unique(as.numeric(stats::quantile(p, probs = seq(0, 1, .1),
                                              names = FALSE, type = 1)))
    if (length(cuts) < 2) {
        warning("All probabilities tied: no calibration bins for ", family)
        next
    }
    bins <- cut(p, breaks = cuts, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE)
    d <- data.table::data.table(bin = bins, y = y, p = p, w = w)
    d <- d[!is.na(bin), .(
        n_respondents = .N,
        weight_total = sum(w),
        predicted = sum(w * p) / sum(w),
        observed = sum(w * y) / sum(w)
    ), by = bin]
    d[, `:=`(family = family, model = model_names[[family]])]
    calibration_rows[[family]] <- d
}
calibration_table <- data.table::rbindlist(calibration_rows, use.names = TRUE)
save_table(calibration_table, "07b_2025_national_calibration_bins")
calibration_axis_top <- min(1, max(0.30, 1.08 * max(calibration_table$predicted,
                                                         calibration_table$observed)))
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(calibration_table,
                     ggplot2::aes(predicted, observed, color = family)) +
    ggplot2::geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0,
                         color = "#CFC0B3", linetype = "dashed") +
    ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1.05) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2.4) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~model, nrow = 1) +
    ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = model_colors) +
    ggplot2::coord_equal(xlim = c(0, calibration_axis_top),
                         ylim = c(0, calibration_axis_top), expand = FALSE) +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "none") +
    ggplot2::labs(title = "2025 national calibration by predicted-risk group",
                  subtitle = "Survey-weighted rates within up to 10 score groups",
                  x = "Mean predicted FMD probability", y = "Observed FMD proportion",
                  caption = "Dotted diagonal = ideal calibration; exploratory bins without CIs.")
show_and_save(p, "07b_2025_national_calibration_curves", 11, 6)
```

## 14. Weighted distributions of predicted probabilities by actual FMD status

Bin-level weight fractions are normalized **separately within each actual outcome class**. The resulting distributions help show overlap, but are not measures of classification accuracy by themselves.

```{r predicted-score-distributions, fig.width=11, fig.height=6, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
score_histograms <- data.table::rbindlist(lapply(families, function(family) {
    p <- eligible[[paste0("prob_", family)]]
    d <- data.table::data.table(
        bin = pmin(39L, as.integer(floor(p * 40))), y = y, w = w)
    d <- d[, .(weight = sum(w)), by = .(bin, y)]
    d[, fraction := weight / sum(weight), by = y]
    d[, `:=`(family = family, model = model_names[[family]],
             midpoint = (bin + 0.5) / 40,
             outcome = ifelse(y == 1, "FMD", "No FMD"))]
    d
}))
save_table(score_histograms, "07b_2025_national_score_distribution_bins")
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(score_histograms,
                     ggplot2::aes(midpoint, fraction, color = outcome)) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1.05) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~model, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y") +
    ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = c("FMD" = positive_color,
                                           "No FMD" = negative_color)) +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(title = "2025 predicted-risk distributions by observed FMD",
                  subtitle = "Survey-weighted percentage distribution within each actual outcome class",
                  x = "Predicted FMD probability", y = "Fraction of outcome class per 0.025 risk bin",
                  color = "Actual FMD")
show_and_save(p, "07b_2025_national_score_distributions", 11, 6)
```

## 15. Comparing probability-based metrics

AUROC and average precision are **higher-is-better**; Brier score and log loss are **lower-is-better**. These are displayed in separate panels with independent scales to avoid misleading direct numerical comparisons.

```{r probability-metrics-dashboard, fig.width=11, fig.height=6, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
prob_metric_long <- data.table::melt(
    metric_table,
    id.vars = c("family", "model"),
    measure.vars = c("weighted_auroc", "weighted_average_precision",
                     "weighted_brier", "weighted_logloss"),
    variable.name = "metric", value.name = "score")
prob_metric_long[, metric := factor(metric,
    levels = c("weighted_auroc", "weighted_average_precision",
               "weighted_brier", "weighted_logloss"),
    labels = c("AUROC ↑", "Average precision ↑", "Brier score ↓", "Log loss ↓"))]
prob_metric_long[, model := factor(model, levels = unname(model_names[families]))]
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(prob_metric_long,
                     ggplot2::aes(model, score, fill = family)) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(width = .66) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = sprintf("%.4f", score)),
                       vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~metric, nrow = 2, scales = "free_y") +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = model_colors) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, .20))) +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "none",
                   axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 18, hjust = 1)) +
    ggplot2::labs(title = "2025 national model performance summary",
                  subtitle = "One eligible sample, same frozen predictions, survey-weighted",
                  x = NULL, y = NULL,
                  caption = "Panels have independent vertical scales and must be interpreted separately.")
show_and_save(p, "07b_2025_national_probability_metrics_dashboard", 11, 6)
```

## 17. H1: Paired 95% confidence interval for Brier-score improvement

**Research hypothesis H1:** Previously trained models improve 2025 probability prediction of FMD relative to the *frozen historical-prevalence-only* reference.

This section uses the **same respondents**, **same weights**, and **same sampled PSUs** for both models in every replicate. The paired outcome-level quantity is

\[
\Delta = \operatorname{Brier}(\text{historical prevalence only})
       - \operatorname{Brier}(\text{2023-selected classifier}).
\]

**Positive improvement indicates lower probability error** for the selected classifier.
Relative improvement is \(100\Delta/\operatorname{Brier}(\text{baseline})\).

This repeats the fixed-model, stratified-PSU bootstrap used in the main `07_Evaluate_2025` notebook, but only for this **single paired Brier difference**. It is computationally efficient because it aggregates the frozen respondent errors to PSUs before drawing replicates. It *does not* refit the classifier, retune thresholds, or estimate uncertainty from training and calibration. Single-PSU strata are held fixed. Therefore the percentile intervals are **approximate, exploratory survey-sampling intervals**, not a complete CDC-design uncertainty analysis.

```{r h1-paired-brier-bootstrap, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Required objects supplied by earlier notebook sections:
# scored, eligible, selected, y, w, and project helpers.
# A frozen historical baseline is essential: do not replace it with 2025
# observed prevalence, which would use the evaluation outcomes to set the score.
stopifnot(all(c("YEAR", "STATE", "STRAT", "PSU", "RAW_WEIGHT") %in% names(scored)))
if (anyNA(scored[, .(YEAR, STATE, STRAT, PSU, RAW_WEIGHT)])) {
    stop("Missing design identifiers. Resolve before calculating the paired CI.")
}
if (!exists("selected") || is.null(selected$chosen_family) ||
    is.null(selected$training_prevalence)) {
    stop("Cannot find the frozen 2023 selection and historical training prevalence.")
}
chosen_family <- as.character(selected$chosen_family)
if (!chosen_family %in% families) stop("Unrecognized frozen selected family.")
historical_p <- as.numeric(selected$training_prevalence)
if (length(historical_p) != 1L || !is.finite(historical_p) ||
    historical_p <= 0 || historical_p >= 1) {
    stop("Invalid frozen historical training prevalence.")
}
p_selected <- eligible[[paste0("prob_", chosen_family)]]
if (length(p_selected) != length(y) || anyNA(p_selected)) {
    stop("Selected model probabilities do not align with eligible outcomes.")
}

# Build the complete 2025 PSU sampling frame FIRST (before removing outcomes).
psu_frame <- unique(scored[, .(YEAR, STATE, STRAT, PSU)])
psu_frame[, stratum_key := paste(YEAR, STATE, STRAT, sep = "_")]
psu_frame[, psu_key := paste(YEAR, STATE, STRAT, PSU, sep = "_")]
psu_frame[, psu_index := seq_len(.N)]
strata_indices <- split(psu_frame$psu_index, psu_frame$stratum_key)
singleton_count <- sum(lengths(strata_indices) == 1L)

elig_key <- paste(eligible$YEAR, eligible$STATE, eligible$STRAT,
                  eligible$PSU, sep = "_")
psu_index <- match(elig_key, psu_frame$psu_key)
if (anyNA(psu_index)) stop("Some eligible outcomes have no matching full-sample PSU.")

# Frozen, PAIRED individual Brier losses; both errors are evaluated on each row.
base_error <- (historical_p - y)^2
model_error <- (p_selected - y)^2
aggregate_psu <- data.table::data.table(
    psu_index = psu_index,
    respondent_w = w,
    baseline_error_total = w * base_error,
    selected_error_total = w * model_error
)[, .(
    weighted_n = sum(respondent_w),
    baseline_loss = sum(baseline_error_total),
    selected_loss = sum(selected_error_total)
), by = psu_index]

psu_n <- nrow(psu_frame)
psu_weights <- numeric(psu_n)
psu_baseline <- numeric(psu_n)
psu_selected <- numeric(psu_n)
psu_weights[aggregate_psu$psu_index] <- aggregate_psu$weighted_n
psu_baseline[aggregate_psu$psu_index] <- aggregate_psu$baseline_loss
psu_selected[aggregate_psu$psu_index] <- aggregate_psu$selected_loss

# For each draw, compute both Brier scores using THE SAME PSU multiplicities.
paired_brier <- function(psu_multiplicity) {
    denominator <- sum(psu_multiplicity * psu_weights)
    if (!is.finite(denominator) || denominator <= 0) {
        return(c(baseline = NA_real_, selected = NA_real_,
                 absolute_gain = NA_real_, relative_gain_pct = NA_real_))
    }
    b0 <- sum(psu_multiplicity * psu_baseline) / denominator
    b1 <- sum(psu_multiplicity * psu_selected) / denominator
    diff <- b0 - b1
    c(baseline = b0, selected = b1, absolute_gain = diff,
      relative_gain_pct = 100 * diff / b0)
}

h1_point <- paired_brier(rep(1L, psu_n))
# Same RNG seed and PSU resampling procedure used in Notebook 07.
n_boot <- if (exists("psu_bootstrap_replicates")) {
    as.integer(psu_bootstrap_replicates)
} else 399L
if (length(n_boot) != 1L || is.na(n_boot) || n_boot < 30L) {
    stop("At least 30 valid PSU replicates are required for this exploratory CI.")
}
set.seed(if (exists("seed")) as.integer(seed) + 707L else 20260707L)
h1_boot <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_boot, ncol = length(h1_point),
                  dimnames = list(NULL, names(h1_point)))
for (b in seq_len(n_boot)) {
    multiplicity <- integer(psu_n)
    for (ids in strata_indices) {
        if (length(ids) == 1L) {
            multiplicity[ids] <- 1L
        } else {
            multiplicity[ids] <- tabulate(
                sample.int(length(ids), size = length(ids), replace = TRUE),
                nbins = length(ids))
        }
    }
    h1_boot[b, ] <- paired_brier(multiplicity)
}
if (!all(is.finite(h1_boot))) stop("Non-finite PSU bootstrap results.")
q <- function(x) as.numeric(stats::quantile(x, c(0.025, 0.975), names = FALSE))
abs_ci <- q(h1_boot[, "absolute_gain"])
rel_ci <- q(h1_boot[, "relative_gain_pct"])

h1_table <- data.table::data.table(
    evaluation_year = 2025L,
    selected_family = chosen_family,
    respondents = length(y),
    historical_prevalence = historical_p,
    baseline_brier = unname(h1_point["baseline"]),
    selected_brier = unname(h1_point["selected"]),
    absolute_brier_gain = unname(h1_point["absolute_gain"]),
    absolute_ci_lower = abs_ci[1], absolute_ci_upper = abs_ci[2],
    relative_brier_gain_pct = unname(h1_point["relative_gain_pct"]),
    relative_ci_lower_pct = rel_ci[1], relative_ci_upper_pct = rel_ci[2],
    paired_ci_excludes_zero = abs_ci[1] > 0 || abs_ci[2] < 0,
    bootstrap_psu_replicates = n_boot,
    singleton_strata_held_fixed = singleton_count,
    ci_method = "Paired, stratified PSU percentile bootstrap; frozen predictions"
)
print(h1_table)
save_table(h1_table, "07b_2025_h1_paired_brier_ci")

cat(sprintf("\nH1 slide-ready: historical Brier %.5f; %s Brier %.5f\n",
            h1_table$baseline_brier, chosen_family, h1_table$selected_brier))
cat(sprintf("Absolute improvement %.5f; approximate paired 95%% CI [%.5f, %.5f]\n",
            h1_table$absolute_brier_gain, h1_table$absolute_ci_lower,
            h1_table$absolute_ci_upper))
cat(sprintf("Relative reduction %.1f%%; approximate paired 95%% CI [%.1f%%, %.1f%%]\n",
            h1_table$relative_brier_gain_pct,
            h1_table$relative_ci_lower_pct, h1_table$relative_ci_upper_pct))
cat("Note: CI reflects sampling uncertainty with fixed models; not all sources of uncertainty.\n")
```

## 18. H1 presentation figures: Brier comparison and improvement CI

```{r h1-brier-comparison, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.8, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
brier_compare <- data.frame(
    model = factor(c("Historical prevalence", "Selected logistic regression"),
                   levels = c("Historical prevalence", "Selected logistic regression")),
    brier = c(h1_table$baseline_brier, h1_table$selected_brier),
    label = sprintf("%.5f", c(h1_table$baseline_brier, h1_table$selected_brier))
)
# The figure label follows the actual selected family if it isn't logistic.
if (chosen_family != "logistic") {
    levels(brier_compare$model)[2] <- paste("Selected", model_names[[chosen_family]])
}
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(brier_compare, ggplot2::aes(model, brier, fill = model)) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(width = .54) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = label), vjust = -0.35, size = 5) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = c("#B9A48E", "#2D9E98")) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max(brier_compare$brier) * 1.16)) +
    atg_theme() + ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "none") +
    ggplot2::labs(title = "H1 | 2025 Brier score: selected model vs historical baseline",
                  subtitle = "Same 2025 respondents, survey-weighted | Lower is better",
                  x = NULL, y = "Brier score (mean squared probability error)")
show_and_save(p, "07b_2025_h1_brier_baseline_comparison", 8, 4.8)

```{r h1-relative-improvement-ci, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=4.2, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
plot_ci <- data.frame(
    comparison = "Selected model vs historical baseline",
    gain = h1_table$relative_brier_gain_pct,
    lower = h1_table$relative_ci_lower_pct,
    upper = h1_table$relative_ci_upper_pct
)
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(plot_ci, ggplot2::aes(x = comparison, y = gain)) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#BE8D6E", linetype = "dashed") +
    ggplot2::geom_pointrange(ggplot2::aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                             color = "#2D9E98", linewidth = 1.3, size = 0.8) +
    ggplot2::coord_flip() +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = function(z) paste0(format(z, trim=TRUE), "%")) +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(title = "H1 | Reduction in 2025 Brier error",
                  subtitle = sprintf("%.1f%% reduction; approx. paired 95%% CI [%.1f%%, %.1f%%]",
                                     plot_ci$gain, plot_ci$lower, plot_ci$upper),
                  x = NULL, y = "Relative reduction in squared probability error",
                  caption = "Approx. 95% stratified-PSU percentile interval; frozen models and baseline.\nNo training or calibration uncertainty included.")
show_and_save(p, "07b_2025_h1_relative_brier_gain_ci", 8.5, 4.2)
```

**Suggested H1 slide footer:** *Survey-weighted 2025 BRFSS; paired, approximate 95% stratified-PSU bootstrap interval with fixed model predictions. Out-of-time, post-hoc evaluation.*

**Interpretation rule:** If the interval for the **absolute improvement** excludes zero on the positive side, you can say the sampled-year evidence favors better probability accuracy than the frozen historical reference *under the stated resampling assumptions*. Do not claim future individual FMD prediction, formal causal evidence, or proof of operational screening readiness.
